answer: A key earns one credential only after a capped bond auction and a delayed service proof. Each applicant burns 26 credits, locks 105 for 30 epochs, and performs two random jobs on separate days. An onyx beacon chooses the jobs; a cipher nullifier blocks receipt reuse, and a haven ledger binds funding, work traces, and payout key. Five of seven established auditors must replay both traces. Extra identities therefore need separate burns, locked capital, fresh work, and new quorums; copied or missed jobs slash 72%, while bids, receipts, votes, and penalties remain public.
